title.english: Chapter 1 - An Examination of the Wise

verses.english:
The wise who nourish a treasury of good qualities
Gather to themselves precious good advice.
The great ocean is a treasury of rivers
To which all running waters descend.
verses.chinese:
智者是学问的宝藏,
他们拥有智慧格言;
大海是江河的归宿,
百川都会奔向大海。

verses.english:
People may or may not be knowledgeable, but
The wise are judicious in what to do and what to avoid.
A magnetic stone is able to extract
Iron filings that are mixed with dust.
verses.chinese:
不管本人有无学问,
能辨别是非是智者;
混在灰尘中的铁屑,
磁铁能从灰中吸出。

verses.english:
Skilled in good advice, the wise know,
But foolish people do not.
When the radiance of the sun appears,
Owls become blind.
verses.chinese:
智者用智慧理解格言,
愚人却没有这种能力;
正如阳光普照的时候,
猫头鹰会成瞎子一样。

verses.english:
The wise can eradicate faults,
But the foolish cannot.
The garuda can kill poisonous snakes,
But crows cannot.
verses.chinese:
聪明的人敢于改正错误,
愚蠢的人没有这种勇气;
大鹏敢啄死有毒的巨蛇,
但乌鸦却没有这种能耐。

verses.english:
When the wise become very destitute
Their intelligence grows even stronger.
When the king of beasts becomes hungry
It swiftly attacks the elephant's head.
verses.chinese:
聪明的人即使惨遭挫折,
也能变得更加智慧强大;
正如兽王被饥饿所困时,
仍然能将大象置于死地。

verses.english:
Until the learned are thoroughly questioned,
Their depth cannot be assessed.
Until a drum is beaten by drumsticks,
Its distinction from other drums is unknown.
verses.chinese:
如果对智者不辩又不问,
无法了解其学识的深浅;
如果不用槌子来敲打鼓,
就无法识别与它物有别。

verses.english:
Even if one is to die the next morning, today one must study.
Though one may not become a sage in this life,
Knowledge is safely deposited for future lives,
Just as riches safely deposited can later be reclaimed.
verses.chinese:
明日离世也要学智慧,
尽管今生成不了智者,
如为来世积蓄的资粮,
同今世享用没有区别。

verses.english:
When a person possesses good qualities,
Others spontaneously gather around.
The fragrant flower may be distant,
But bees are drawn like gathering clouds.
verses.chinese:
如果是真正有学问的人,
人们自然从四方来请教;
好像鲜花虽盛开在远方,
蜜蜂会云聚其周围一样。

verses.english:
A single wise person who has fully developed
All good qualities illumines the earth.
But the mean-spirited, like stars,
Even when numerous, cannot illumine.
verses.chinese:
聪明的人爱学所有知识,
精通一门就知晓天下事;
愚蠢的人虽然见多识广,
却像星星缺少灿烂光芒。

verses.english:
Although the wise have immeasurable learning,
They still embrace the lesser knowledge of others.
By means of continuously practicing thus,
They quickly proceed to omniscience.
verses.chinese:
智者虽有渊博的知识,
仍学别人微小的长处,
如果能坚持这种美德,
很快就能成为遍知者。

verses.english:
Though enemies are numerous, when the wise
Are protected by wisdom, how can they be harmed?
Single-handedly, the Brahmin boy of Ujjayini
Triumphed over an entire assembly of foes.
verses.chinese:
智者用智慧来保护自己,
敌人虽很多也无可奈何;
好像乌仗那婆罗门之子,
能够独自战胜敌军一样。

verses.english:
When offensive talk from small minds creates quarrels,
The wise skillfully restore harmony.
The river's turbulence muddies the water,
But the sparkling water-jewel purifies it,
verses.chinese:
愚蠢的人瞎辩是非时,
智者有妙法促成平静;
河水浑浊不清的时候,
净水宝珠能使它清澈。

verses.english:
Howsoever the wise become destitute,
They do not take the path of fools.
Even if thirsty, birds who crave rain
Will not drink water fallen to the ground.
verses.chinese:
智者不管怎么穷困潦倒,
也不会像愚者一样做人,
布谷鸟虽然因饥渴难忍,
也不会吸吮地上的污水。

verses.english:
Even if the wise are deceived,
They are not confused about what they do.
Although ants are sightless,
They are speedier than creatures with eyes.
verses.chinese:
尽管智者遭遇到愚弄,
也不会在大事上糊涂;
虽然说蚂蚁没有眼睛,
仍比有眼睛的跑得快。

verses.english:
When two wise people engage in discussion,
Further worthy wisdom can arise.
By mixing turmeric with borax,
Another color is produced.
verses.chinese:
两个聪明人在一起商量,
肯定会想出更好的办法;
把姜黄和硼砂配在一起,
会调出更美的色彩一样。

verses.english:
The noble wise ones who have gathered merit
Will be victorious over all, even if they stand alone.
The lion, king of beasts, and universal monarchs
Have no need of allies for their rule.
verses.chinese:
智慧和福泽兼备的人,
独自能战胜一切敌人;
如兽王雄狮和转轮王,
不需朋友的帮助一样。

verses.english:
When skilled in method, why should it be hard
To employ even the great as servants?
The garuda, though very powerful,
Is ridden by the golden-clad one.
verses.chinese:
假若能善于运筹帷幄,
役使强者也并非很难;
揭楼罗虽然本领高强,
却成了毗纽天的坐骑。

verses.english:
Wisdom is what achieves happiness
In both this and future lives.
Prince Chandra's wisdom protected King Sudasa
In this lifetime and those to come.
verses.chinese:
欲获今生来世的安乐,
只能依靠智慧的力量;
达瓦王子用智慧力量,
救了真桑的今生来世。

verses.english:
Though people may be very brave and strong,
Without wisdom they cannot become heroes.
Though people may become very wealthy,
Without virtues how can their wealth endure?
verses.chinese:
尽管既英勇又顽强,
若非智者难得吉祥;
尽管多么富有钱财,
若无福分很难长久。

verses.english:
Distinct good and bad are clear to all,
But the wise distinguish them when mixed.
Anyone can take milk from the cow,
But swans separate milk from water.
verses.chinese:
谁都会知道是非有所不同,
唯有智者能辨认是非之异。
人人都会从母牛身上挤奶,
只有天鹅才会从水中分奶。

verses.english:
When they are commanded,
Even animals can understand.
Those who know what to do
Without being directed are wise.
verses.chinese:
对于琐事既嘱咐又催促,
就是牲畜也能有所领会;
根本用不着嘱咐和催促,
能心领神会者便是智者。

verses.english:
If one has wisdom, one can understand others
From just their demeanor, even if they say nothing.
Even without eating a crab apple
One can tell its taste by its color.
verses.chinese:
对于聪明人用不着多讲,
从态度上就知有所想法;
尼泊尔的石榴不用尝试,
仅观颜色就能知其滋味。

verses.english:
The wise command more respect in other lands
Than they do in their homeland.
How could a jewel, readily sold in other regions,
Be prized on the ocean isle where jewels abound?
verses.chinese:
若智者离开自己的家乡,
到别处更受人们的敬仰;
如珠宝只有在外地畅销,
孤岛上永远不会有销路。

verses.english:
Learning entails hardship;
Living at ease, one cannot become wise.
Due to attachment to small pleasures
One cannot attain great happiness.
verses.chinese:
成就智者之路充满艰辛,
贪图安乐者成不了智者,
只会留恋微小的安乐者;
不可能得到更大的幸福。

verses.english:
One may be weak, but if one has wisdom,
What can a powerful enemy do?
Although the king of beasts was strong,
He was put to death by a clever rabbit.
verses.chinese:
智者尽管非常弱小,
也使劲敌无可奈何;
兽王虽然强大无比,
却被智兔以谋取命。

verses.english:
When one is able to behave harmoniously
With other beings, then one is wise.
Do animals not also abide compatibly
In groups of their own kind?
verses.chinese:
懂得同别人和睦相处,
才能算作是有智之士;
就算是四蹄动物之类,
不也是能够以类相聚?

verses.english:
Know the difference between wise people and fools:
The wise investigate a situation carefully
Before taking action on what needs to be done;
A fool's approach is to act before thinking.
verses.chinese:
从事前的分析研究中
可以辨别出智愚之别,
事后才勉强分析事因,
那只能是愚蠢的行径。

verses.english:
When one knows what the wise investigate
One is counted among the wise.
A fool may be skilled in assessing a cow's age
But that is not so valuable an attainment.
verses.chinese:
谙熟智者所辨的知识,
才能算作真正的学者,
鉴别牛龄大小的学问,
不该算作最高的学问。

verses.english:
As the ocean is not filled up by rivers,
The king's treasury is not sated by wealth,
Sense desires are not quenched through indulgence,
And the wise are never slaked with good advice.
verses.chinese:
大海永不以水为患,
国库永不有财为余,
常人不会嫌享受多,
智者不会嫌格言多。

verses.english:
Wise people fully accept good advice
Even if it comes from children.
For fragrant perfumes to be produced,
Musk is taken from the scent glands of deer.
verses.chinese:
格言即使出自小孩之口,
智者也会把它全部吸收;
如果能散发芬芳的气味,
麝香长在兽脐也会取出。

title.english: Chapter 2 - An Examination of the Noble

verses.english:
The good qualities of noble people
Are always acclaimed by the wise.
The fragrance of white sandalwood is spread
Throughout the ten directions by the wind.
verses.chinese:
凡是属于高尚的知识,
圣哲常常会特意宣扬;
玛拉雅山区的檀香味,
微风会把它传送十方。

verses.english:
When sages are installed as rulers.
There will be achievement and happiness.
If a jewel is offered to the victory banner's tip,
The wise say virtue then reigns over the land.
verses.chinese:
委派高尚的人去做官,
既能成事又能享受福;
如果把宝石供于幢顶,
智者们称颂惠泽一方。

verses.english:
Once hurt by a despotic ruler,
People fondly recall the Dharma king.
A person stricken by a bout of fever
Thinks only of the water from melting snow.
verses.chinese:
被其他暴君残害的时候,
就会特别怀念转轮法王;
当众生在瘟疫中痛苦时,
时常会想到雪山的圣水。

verses.english:
For those harmed by unprincipled rulers,
The ways of Dharma kings are especially protective.
Those afflicted by evil spirits
Are protected by tantric adepts.
verses.chinese:
遭受暴君迫害的时候,
人间法王更保护属民;
惨遭恶魔缠身的时候,
金刚咒师就会来保护。

verses.english:
Noble people abstain from even minor wrongdoings,
But coarse people fail to avoid even major ones.
Miniscule dust particles are removed from yogurt,
But grains of yeast are specially added to beer.
verses.chinese:
高尚者有点罪恶就会放弃,
卑劣者罪恶再大仍就行使;
酸奶里有点浮尘就要清除,
酒糟里还要多加些酒曲子。

verses.english:
Even when noble people become impoverished,
Their behavior remains distinctly honorable.
Even if a firebrand is pointed downward,
One sees the flames continue to blaze upward.
verses.chinese:
贤者虽然惨遭厄运,
行为仍然光明磊落;
火把虽然倾倒朝下,
火焰始终向上燃烧。

verses.english:
Noble people, even when living far away,
Care for their friends by helping from afar.
The buildup of great heavy clouds in the sky
Makes the earth's crops yield a rich harvest.
verses.chinese:
高尚的人随住在远方,
也会保护自己的属民;
正因天空的浓云密雨,
才能使庄稼特别茁壮。

verses.english:
One's reputation brings pleasure while one is alive;
Merit brings happiness in future lives.
Mere riches that do not include these two
Are unable to gladden the wise.
verses.chinese:
荣誉是今生的福源,
功德是来世的资粮,
除此两外尽凭钱财,
绝不会使智者欢欣。

verses.english:
Those who can see far into the future,
Have great forbearance and conscientiousness,
Tremendous perseverance and competence
They can become leaders even if they are servants.
verses.chinese:
如果时常从长远着眼,
谨慎小心并任劳任怨,
勤奋学习并稳重机灵,
即便是奴仆也能为官。

verses.english:
Those who delight in always being charitable
Have reputations that rise like the wind;
More numerous than beggars who gather around
Are those who wish to give offerings.
verses.chinese:
经常乐善好施的人,
其声誉会四处传扬;
如穷困乞丐聚集时,
愿意馈赠者会更多。

verses.english:
Willingly accepting contempt from the mean-spirited
To whom they have given good advice that goes unpracticed
And not forgetting even small favors bestowed on them
Are superb distinguishing features of extraordinary people.
verses.chinese:
做了施舍却不求回报,
能够容忍贱人的侮辱;
受恩虽小却永不忘记,
这是伟人高尚的标志。

verses.english:
The good qualities of the noble, though hidden,
Are apparent to everyone in the world.
Even when the jasmine flower is well-covered
Its fragrance permeates everywhere.
verses.chinese:
圣者虽不爱炫耀学问,
他的美名却到处颂扬;
豆蔻花虽被严密裹藏,
它的芳香却飘溢四方。

verses.english:
A king is great merely in his own country,
But sages are respected wherever they go.
Usually a flower is decoration only for a day,
But crown ornaments are venerated universally.
verses.chinese:
国王仅能受国人尊敬,
圣人却能使世人敬仰;
花朵仅是一天的装饰,
顶髻宝却能永受供奉。

verses.english:
Plentiful fruit indicates a matured tree,
Beautiful tail feathers indicate a tamed peacock,
Swift journeys indicate a fine tamed horse,
And a noble person's calm manner indicates wisdom.
verses.chinese:
弯曲的树木果实累累,
文静的孔雀尾屏优美,
温顺的骏马鹏程万里,
谦虚的智者富有智慧。

verses.english:
Noble and ordinary people may receive help equally,
But their gratitude in response is not the same.
Seeds make no difference to the fields,
Yet there are vast differences in crops.
verses.chinese:
给圣人和常人做同样的事,
反还的回报却有天壤之别;
在田野里播下同样的种子,
长出来的庄稼却相差很大。

verses.english:
When assistance is given to extraordinary people,
There are fruitful results even if help is slight.
One who gave a single sour fruit to the king
Was regarded as equal to the king's son.
verses.chinese:
如果给圣人做了件好事,
尽管微小也能得到回报;
正如只因赠送一颗山楂,
法轮王就待他亲如弟子。

verses.english:
Good ancestral lineage is protected by proper conduct,
But when behavior degenerates, ancestry is irrelevant.
People appreciate the fragrance of white sandalwood,
But who is interested in its ashes?
verses.chinese:
高贵种姓靠行为来护持,
品行堕落种姓也失真意,
虽然人人爱檀香的芬芳,
烧成灰炭就没有人留恋。

verses.english:
Though great people may be impoverished for awhile,
They need not experience any anguish in that.
The moon may be briefly eclipsed,
But an instant later it is released.
verses.chinese:
伟人暂时惨遭到挫折,
也不必为此感到悲伤;
月亮暂时被罗睺吞食,
顷刻之间能恢复圆满。

verses.english:
When great ones bestow love on their enemies
Those enemies come under their sway.
Widely respected, they care for everyone;
Such a ruler commands the allegiance of all.
verses.chinese:
若伟人对敌待以慈悲,
敌人会变成他的属民;
慈众又能得众人敬仰,
自然就会推他为国王。

verses.english:
No matter how impoverished the sages become,
They will not eat food tainted with wrongdoing.
Even though a lion is hungry,
It will not consume what is disgusting and unclean.
verses.chinese:
圣人尽管惨遭了厄运,
不会食用罪恶的食物;
百兽王宁可饿着肚子,
不会食用肮脏的食物。

verses.english:
Even when the lives of sages are endangered,
How could they abandon their superb character?
Even testing gold nuggets by burning or cutting
Does not diminish their golden color.
verses.chinese:
圣人尽管会失去生命,
绝不抛弃善良的本性;
真金不管怎样来提炼,
也不会损伤灿烂本色。

verses.english:
Although coarse people get angry with them,
How could noble people retaliate in anger?
Even though the jackal barks arrogantly,
The king of beasts responds with compassion.
verses.chinese:
卑劣之徒向高尚者发怒,
高尚的人不会以怒相报:
豺狼发出傲慢的嗥叫时,
兽王却对它以慈悲为怀。

verses.english:
People seek defects in extraordinary people,
But not in coarse individuals.
People examine the flaws of gems carefully,
But who would so scrutinize a fire brand?
verses.chinese:
人们对圣人苛以找茬,
对常人却能顺其自然;
如只鉴别宝石的瑕玷,
也不探究木炭的裂纹。

verses.english:
Not to be pleased by praise,
Nor displeased by criticism,
And to maintain properly their good qualities:
These are characteristics of noble people.
verses.chinese:
不会被赞美而高兴,
也不因辱骂而愤怒;
能始终保持好品质,
这才是圣人的本色。

verses.english:
Genuine wealth is not obtained
By coercion or wrongdoing.
Dogs and cats gorging themselves with food
Is a classic case of shamelessness.
verses.chinese:
靠罪恶和武力获得的财富,
自然不会变成真正的财富;
猫狗之徒虽然吃饱了肚子,
照样会干一些无耻的行径。

verses.english:
When prosperity comes to their subjects,
That is the sign of the greatness of kings.
Does not the decorative harness adorning horses
Also make handsome the riders themselves?
verses.chinese:
能使下属幸福圆满,
方能显示王者风范;
正如为马装饰瓔珞,
方显主人光彩一样。

verses.english:
To whatever extent rulers endeavor
To govern their subjects with kindness,
To that extent the citizenry strives
To fulfill their civic duties.
verses.chinese:
担任一方官职的人,
若能善待下属民众,
民众也以善愿着眼,
同样为他诚心做事。

verses.english:
In places where extraordinary people reside,
Who would consider others as wise?
When the sun rises in the sky,
The stars are many but none are seen.
verses.chinese:
圣人弘扬圣道的地方,
一般学者不会被敬仰;
好像太阳高现晴空时,
星星再多也失去踪影。

title.english: Chapter 3 - An Examination of the Foolish

verses.english:
Bad people can acquire wealth, but then
Their behavior truly degenerates.
No matter how one tries to reverse a waterfall,
It is well known it can only flow downward.
verses.chinese:
尽管恶人发了横财,
行为变得更加可恶,
不管怎样阻挡瀑布,
始终只能往下流淌。

verses.english:
Good conduct may occur in coarse people,
But it is an instance of artificiality.
Glass may be colored to look like a jewel,
But when it touches water, its true color shows.
verses.chinese:
尽管恶人也会有善行,
只是暂时伪装的行为;
涂有宝石色彩的玻璃,
遇到水就会暴露真相。

verses.english:
Although a fool may do something good,
It's a lucky coincidence, not deliberate.
The silk thread from a silkworm's saliva
Does not come about through skill.
verses.chinese:
愚人有时也能完成些事情,
那是依靠运气而不是能力;
尽管蚕虫也能够吐丝抽线,
那是本能而并非精于纺织。

verses.english:
Things that the great achieve with great effort,
Bad people destroy in an instant.
Crops for which farmers toil months and years,
Hailstorms destroy in an instant.
verses.chinese:
伟人努力达成的协议,
恶人瞬间就能够毁掉;
农夫整年耕耘的庄稼,
冰雹瞬间便化为灰烬。

verses.english:
Bad people usually attribute to others
Any faults they themselves possess.
Crows smear their filth-eating beaks
Vigorously over other clean places.
verses.chinese:
卑鄙之人把自己的过失,
往往会推到别人的身上;
正如乌鸦把食脏的嘴唇,
往往会寻找干净处磨蹭。

verses.english:
When responsibilities are given to a fool,
Things deteriorate, then get even worse.
It is said that because a fox was appointed king,
He tormented his followers and was himself killed.
verses.chinese:
如果让愚人去办些事,
既毁事情又毁了自己;
据说狐狸被拥立为王,
众兽受苦自己也丧命。

verses.english:
While the ignorant are wishing for happiness,
Their deeds bring them only suffering.
Some people possessed by evil spirits
Are seen to commit suicide to ease their pain.
verses.chinese:
愚蠢的人苦苦追求幸福,
但只能办些痛苦的事情;
正如被病魔缠身心的人,
为消灾选择了自尽一样。

verses.english:
Some straightforward dull people ruin themselves,
And some bring destruction to others.
Straight trees in the forest are sought out and cut,
And straight arrows are used to kill others.
verses.chinese:
愚蠢而且憨厚的人,
不会伤己就会伤人,
挺拔的树木被砍伐,
锋利的弓箭会夺命。

verses.english:
Always ignoring the interests of others
Is to behave in the same way as cattle.
Is it not possible even for animals
Merely to acquire food and drink?
verses.chinese:
时常不愿替别人着想,
他的行为同牲畜类似;
只会寻找自己的吃喝,
这是牲畜也有的本能。

verses.english:
Those oblivious to what helps or harms,
Who do not think carefully or listen to others,
And aspire only to a full stomach -
They are nothing but hairless pigs.
verses.chinese:
不会辨别有益和无益,
不愿增长智慧和见闻,
死心塌地只追求吃喝,
纯系一头无毛的猪猡。

verses.english:
Those who are delighted and amused amid fools,
But intimidated and shy with the wise,
Though lacking a hump or dewlap,
Are actually cattle with upper teeth.
verses.chinese:
在愚人中间爱出风头,
在智者面前畏惧折腰;
尽管没有爬行的身躯,
却是有上牙齿的黄牛。

verses.english:
Those who run around seeking food and drink
Yet flee when assigned important duties,
Even if they can tell stories and joke around,
They are just old dogs without tails.
verses.chinese:
常常跟着吃喝团团转,
委托办点善事却溜走,
尽管能在人前装模样,
仍是条无尾的赖皮狗。

verses.english:
Hoof prints are easily filled with water,
Small treasuries are easily filled with wealth,
Small fields are easily planted with seeds, and
Small minds are easily contented with knowledge.
verses.chinese:
马蹄窝容易被水灌满,
小仓库容易被物装满,
小块田地也容易播种,
学识浅薄者容易自满。

verses.english:
Even if he is important, an arrogant fool
Who makes promises is disastrous.
By giving away a one-step measure of land,
Bali lost the three realms.
verses.chinese:
傲慢并且容易食言的傻瓜,
尽管拥有强大势力也会垮;
轻敌的阿修罗应人小块地,
却失去了三界所有的土地。

verses.english:
Small-minded people with malice in their hearts
Signal their intent before giving harm.
Even vicious dogs, upon seeing an enemy,
Emit a growl before biting.
verses.chinese:
如果小人存心要报复,
制造危害前先有态度;
如果恶狗见到了敌人,
咬人前必会狂吠几声。

verses.english:
Fools know the hassle of amassing wealth
But not the enjoyment of putting it to use.
Time and again they wander around seeking riches;
In their avarice they are just like mice.
verses.chinese:
愚人能经受敛财的苦楚,
可是很少有享受的福分,
他虽然有些积钱的法子,
却还是一只过街的老鼠。

verses.english:
Amid fools, a man with a leashed monkey
Is much more respected than the wise.
The organ grinder is honored with money and food,
But the wise person leaves empty-handed.
verses.chinese:
用愚人的眼光看智者,
不会比耍猴者更高明,
玩耍猴子者食财兼得,
智者却只能空手而归。

verses.english:
People devoid of good personal qualities
Are particularly hostile to those who have them.
A crop grown in winter in a snowy land
Is proclaimed to be a bad omen.
verses.chinese:
不学无术的庸人们,
非常嫉恨有智慧者,
如果冬雪里出禾苗,
自然会传成是恶兆。

verses.english:
Poorly trained people have special disdain
For those who are properly schooled.
On some islands, those without goiters
Are criticized for stunted limbs.
verses.chinese:
有一些歪门邪道的人,
常嘲笑真才实学的人;
正如某些孤岛上的人,
竟然把无瘤者当废物。

verses.english:
Those who do their work defectively
Disparage others who complete their tasks.
When they venture to the land of the one-legged ones,
Two-legged people are not considered human.
verses.chinese:
始终想祸乱礼仪的人,
偏偏要欺凌护礼的人,
正如在名叫阻达地方,
只有双脚的人不算人。

verses.english:
Some who perform their work improperly
Rebuke those who do their tasks well.
Dog-headed people mock the honorable
By calling them insulting names.
verses.chinese:
行为古怪不守规矩的人,
非常憎恨行为规矩的人。
竟把长得狗头狗脑的人,
反会被热嘲冷讽为美女。

verses.english:
Those who gain food and riches from wrong livelihood
Criticize those who are wise but poor.
Old monkeys, when they behold human beings,
Burst out laughing and say, "They have no tails!"
verses.chinese:
靠倒行逆流来谋生者,
会恶意辱骂布衣学者;
如猴子抓住了人类后,
反而会嘲笑没有尾巴。

verses.english:
If oppressed by karma, a wise person
May wander among fools.
The sweet and fragrant mallika flower,
Borne by the wind, is trampled into rubbish.
verses.chinese:
如果惨遭命运的拨弄,
智者也会陷入愚人中;
如同大风吹散的茉莉,
香味就在垃圾中耗尽。

verses.english:
Zealously clinging to their faults
Yet never retaining any exemplary qualities,
Bad people, like strainers,
Catch debris and let pass what is pure.
verses.chinese:
极力追随歪门邪道,
正法明道不问不敬;
恶人就像漏勺一样,
只淀渣滓漏掉精华。

verses.english:
Those with no sense to tell right from wrong
Stand outside the ranks of the wise.
Those absorbed in talk of food and riches
Are referred to as two-legged cows.
verses.chinese:
没有辨别是非的智慧,
在学者面前藏头露尾,
只知道谈论吃饱发财,
是个直立行走的畜生。

verses.english:
Even when many small minds gather together
They can achieve nothing important.
Even when many twigs are bound together,
They cannot support a house beam.
verses.chinese:
庸俗的人聚集得再多,
也不能成就一件大事;
如芨芨草捆绑得再多,
也不用作大厦的栋梁。

verses.english:
Things may be achieved without investigation,
But who would consider that wise?
Insects leave tracks that look like letters,
But they themselves are not literate.
verses.chinese:
没有经过研究办成事,
不会有人把他当智者;
就像虫子蚕食的花纹,
貌似文字却非真文字。

verses.english:
Sensual talk of the weak-minded,
Magnificent but dull-witted horses,
Swords that fall on the battleground:
It is unsure whose allies these will be.
verses.chinese:
愚蠢的人发出的狂言,
没有经过驯服的烈马,
丢失在战场上的宝剑,
不可以断言对谁有利。

verses.english:
Even if ignorant fools are numerous,
They succumb to the power of their foes.
A large herd of many strong elephants
Was tamed by a single wise rabbit.
verses.chinese:
没有智慧的蠢材再多,
也容易会被敌人制服,
正如成群结队的大象,
会听从慧兔摆布一样。

verses.english:
Though the ignorant may have wealth,
They generally gain little benefit from it.
Though the wish-fulfilling cow has milk,
There is not much for its calf to drink.
verses.chinese:
若非依靠智慧的财富,
多半对己带不来好处;
正如奶牛体内的乳汁,
牛犊只能偶尔才吃到。

verses.english:
It is uncertain whether or not
Even the wise would be honored by fools.
When the bright sun shines
Do evil spirits not flee?
verses.chinese:
愚蠢的人遇到了智者,
不能肯定会以礼相待;
灿烂阳光虽惠及万物,
妖魔鬼怪会躲到暗处。

verses.english:
When do fools who have accumulated wealth
Ever think of their friends and relatives?
Solely absorbed in wrongdoing and cursing,
They get rich and then die, just like mice.
verses.chinese:
愚蠢的人只会拼命赚钱,
绝不会顾得上亲朋好友;
如遭受痛苦和诅咒之后,
只能会身亡留财如老鼠。

verses.english:
How can those with special qualities
Be respected in a group of bad people?
Even lamplight does not shine forth
In places where poisonous snakes live.
verses.chinese:
在歹徒们聚集的地方,
不会敬仰有学问的人;
在毒蛇群出没的地方,
火把虽亮却不会发光。

verses.english:
Though greedy people may have wealth,
Their bad karma renders them powerless to enjoy it.
In the season when grapes are ripe for eating,
The didi bird's mouth is always sore.
verses.chinese:
只有钱财而没有福分,
吝啬鬼无法享受幸福;
当葡萄成熟该享用时,
可乌鸦会重犯咀疮病。

verses.english:
Those who must always be helped by others
Someday will certainly land in trouble,
As in the well-known story of the turtle
Who was carried off by crows, and then fell to earth.
verses.chinese:
时常需要别人的扶持,
总有一天肯定会垮台;
据说天鹅携带的乌龟,
最终还是摔死在地上。

verses.english:
The marks of a fool are: not knowing good from bad,
Ingratitude, indifference to inspiring biographies,
Understanding things yet persisting with questions,
Cowardice, and blindly following others.
verses.chinese:
不分善恶又忘恩负义,
听到怪论又不会吃惊,
亲眼看见又反复询问,
胆小盲从是愚者特征。

verses.english:
Cowards talk about subduing enemies
And shout loudly seeing them at a distance
But fold their palms when confronting them in battle,
Then speak boastfully after returning home.
verses.chinese:
懦夫只会靠嘴皮功夫,
远处见敌就叫爹喊娘,
上了战场会合掌求饶,
回到家里却耀武扬威。

懦夫在商议时爱称雄,
派出去当差时顾利害,
需要去出征时又装病,
临近战场时会吓破胆。

verses.english:
The small-minded boast of some small victory;
Then when they lose they blame their friends.
In discussion they create dissension
And reveal secrets to others.
verses.chinese:
懦夫稍获胜利就傲慢,
遭到失败就抱怨亲友,
集会讨论时偏会争论,
秘密商议的又要泄密。

verses.english:
They clean their ornamental gear on the battlefield
And hide when the enemy confronts them;
When charging, they terrify ally instead of foe,
And toss their weapons into the enemy's hand.
verses.chinese:
上了战场要整理衣着,
见了敌人就跑回后方,
他是暗藏在内的劲敌,
会把武器偷送给敌人。

列队上阵时赖在后面,
凯旋而归时冲在前面,
见到吃喝就拼死拼活,
遇到困难又溜之大吉。

verses.english:
Although many things can be said
About the characteristics of bad people,
Who would draw water from a filthy well?
What wise person wants to taste vomit?
verses.chinese:
有关恶人的种种特征,
还可罗列出多种恶行,
谁愿挖掘污染的水井,
恶心的更是品尝其味。

verses.english:
Giving a signal while moving one's lips,
Winking when talking about others,
Groaning loudly when stories are being told -
It is a sign of coarseness when such things happen.
verses.chinese:
冥冥嘴唇给人暗示,
说起话来挤眉弄眼,
听讲故事长吁短叹,
这都是庸人的特征。

title.english: Chapter 4 - An Examination of Both the Wise and Foolish

verses.english:
Though coarse people acquire great wealth,
They are still overshadowed by the noble.
As the hungry tiger roars,
The monkey falls from the treetop.
verses.chinese:
尽管卑下的富有钱财,
却能被落魄王孙制服;
如饥饿的老虎一声吼,
猢狲们惊恐得掉下树。

verses.english:
A fool's knowledge shows on the surface,
But a wise person's knowledge is hidden within.
A straw floats on top of the water;
A jewel sinks even when placed on the surface.
verses.chinese:
愚者喜欢卖弄学问,
智者喜欢深藏学问;
麦秸总是漂在水面,
宝石始终沉在海底。

verses.english:
Those with limited knowledge have great pride,
But when they become wise, they are composed.
A small creek babbles incessantly,
But what clamor does the ocean produce?
verses.chinese:
浅薄的人特别傲慢,
智慧的人更趋谦虚;
细流的小径常哗然,
大海从来不会喧嚣。

verses.english:
Coarse people disparage the noble,
But noble people do not belittle anyone.
Though lions treat the foxes well,
The foxes quarrel among themselves.
verses.chinese:
卑下人的喜欢诽谤圣贤,
圣贤的从来不会有此念,
如雄狮会特意保护狐狸,
但狐狸间时常明争暗斗。

verses.english:
Noble people, when angry, are mollified by apology,
But coarse people become even more obstinate.
Solid gold and silver can be melted,
But heating dog turds just creates a foul stench.
verses.chinese:
圣贤的生气时可以缓和,
卑下的生气时越劝越僵,
如金银虽坚硬可以熔化,
但狗屎化了会臭气冲天。

verses.english:
The wise possess all virtuous qualities,
While fools have only shortcomings.
From precious jewels comes whatever one needs;
Poisonous snakes bring only misfortune.
verses.chinese:
智者兼备所有的优点,
愚者仅有满身的缺点;
如宝贝使人吉祥如意,
但毒蛇只会蔓延病毒。

verses.english:
Even in the forest malicious people deteriorate,
Even in the city noble people remain serene.
One sees that forest animals are wild and ferocious,
But the best horses are well-disciplined in town.
verses.chinese:
恶人躲在暗处也会灭亡,
善人居在闹市仍会兴旺,
如山中猛兽时常会发怒,
但闹市良马仍然会驯服。

verses.english:
The excellent observe their own faults,
While the coarse seek faults in others.
Peacocks attend to their own form,
While owls hoot bad omens to others.
verses.chinese:
高尚者常检查自己的过,
邪恶者老挑剔别人的错,
孔雀爱剔洗自身的羽毛,
猫头鹰却总给人带恶兆。

圣者既谦虚又能保护人,
恶者既蛮横又害人害己;
果实累累能使人己双赢,
干枯朽木既焚自又毁人。

verses.english:
When one is wealthy, all are friends,
But if one is poor, all are enemies.
People come from afar to the jeweled isle,
But everyone avoids a dried-up lake.
verses.chinese:
兴旺之时人皆良友,
衰落之时尽成仇敌;
宝岛虽远跋涉来聚,
海水千涸没人光顾。

verses.english:
Fools are happy when acquiring wealth;
Noble people find happiness in giving it all away.
Lepers feel better when they scratch their sores,
But note how the wise dread leprosy.
verses.chinese:
愚者欢喜获得财富,
圣者更爱施舍财物;
癞子抓痒自觉满足,
智者见癞心惊胆战。

verses.english:
Toward those individuals who persecute them,
The great are friendly, but the coarse are abusive.
Though the wind fans the blaze of a forest fire,
It will extinguish the flame of a small lamp.
verses.chinese:
伤害伟人会带来善缘,
危害恶人会吃尽苦头;
燃森林火会被风旺盛,
油灯之火又会被熄灭。

verses.english:
Saying, "These are my friends, those are my foes,"
People of small intelligence pigeonhole others.
The wise love everybody equally,
Since it is hard to ascertain who is helpful.
verses.chinese:
朋友和敌人的区别,
卑下者划分得很清,
伟人却能一视同仁,
因为人人有其用处。

verses.english:
Accomplished people are attracted to knowledge,
But ignorant people are not.
Honey-gathering bees are attracted to flowers,
But ordinary houseflies are not.
verses.chinese:
有学问的只爱知识,
无学问的随心所欲;
采花的蜜蜂爱鲜花,
逐臭的苍蝇无所谓。

verses.english:
The wise shine among the wise,
But how can fools recognize them?
As for sandalwood which is dearer than gold,
Look how fools turn it into charcoal!
verses.chinese:
智者在智者中显风采,
愚人却不能领悟智者;
檀香木虽比黄金贵重,
愚夫却把它烧成木炭。

verses.english:
The wise can investigate things for themselves,
But fools chase after whatever is popular.
When an old dog yelps,
Other dogs run without reason.
verses.chinese:
智者常常靠自己思考,
愚者总是靠追随度日;
正如外面稍有些吵闹,
狗群就会瞎跟着狂吠。

verses.english:
Even when the wise become very poor,
They please others with their good advice.
Even when fools become wealthy,
They consume themselves and others with dispute.
verses.chinese:
尽管智者在危难之中,
仍然以格言安慰别人,
可是愚者若发了横财,
就以争吵来伤人害己。

verses.english:
Some are known to achieve things through talking,
Others silently pursue their objectives.
A mean dog barks at the enemy;
Cats and herons silently ambush their prey.
verses.chinese:
有些人总靠嘴巴办事,
有些人却会实际行动,
恶狗见到敌人就狂吠,
鹰和猫却爱伏击猎物。

对圣者作对也会帮人,
同恶者亲近也会害人;
众神发怒会保护众生,
阎王微笑要人的性命。

verses.english:
Like precious jewels, noble people
Remain unchanged in every respect.
Like a balance scale, bad people
Feel elated or dejected at the slightest change.
verses.chinese:
圣者如同珍贵的宝石,
始终不会发生点劣化;
恶者如同秤金的天平,
稍有轻重就晃动秤杆。

verses.english:
Though friends live far away, they are supportive;
Though unfriendly people live nearby, they are remote.
Though growing in mud, the lotus remains unsoiled
And is always nurtured by the sun.
verses.chinese:
心心相印者虽远也会受益,
同床异梦者再近也要分离;
莲花虽出于泥但一尘不染,
太阳对它却时常关怀之至。

verses.english:
As long as one maintains a sense of shame,
One's personal qualities are like the finest jewels;
But when shame is eclipsed, these qualities
Become partial, and one's speech coarsens.
verses.chinese:
如果有多大的廉耻,
也就有多大的功德,
对羞耻也无所顾忌,
肯定就会臭名昭著。

圣者主动为人指明正道,
贱者询问反会步入歧途;
凌辱佛子也会慈悲为怀,
朝供阎王反而难逃丧命。

verses.english:
It is possible that what helps one
May cause harm to another.
At moonrise the water lily blossoms,
But the lotus flower closes.
verses.chinese:
往往有些好处的事情,
同时也会有一些害处;
月亮高高升起的时候,
莲荷就有对立的反应。

verses.english:
Although a goal may be achieved through wrongdoing,
Why would the wise admire it?
Although something done right may go wrong,
The wise may not feel ashamed.
verses.chinese:
虽说靠罪孽也能成事,
智者却永远不会称赞;
认真办事也可能犯错,
智者会安慰各种过失。

verses.english:
Some discoveries are profitable,
Others turn out adverse.
A pregnant mare increases one's wealth,
But when a mule gets pregnant, it dies.
verses.chinese:
有的额外获得带来利益,
有的蜕变为灾难的源头;
骡马怀驹是增财的前兆,
骡子怀胎只能面临死亡。

verses.english:
Noble people are hard to alienate and easy to reunite;
Coarse people are easy to estrange and hard to reunite.
See the difference between cutting trees to make charcoal
And trying to reconstitute trees from charcoal.
verses.chinese:
圣贤的易合却难分开,
恶劣的易分却难和谐;
树木和木炭作为材料,
砍伐和利用各具其道。

verses.english:
Even the strong have trouble defeating
Those who are weak but cautious.
Even the weak often defeat
Those who are strong but careless.
verses.chinese:
弱小的如果有所警惕,
强大的也就无可奈何;
强大的如果麻痹大意,
会被弱小的以谋毁灭。

verses.english:
Having wealth, one's power increases;
Without wealth, one's power diminishes.
The rich mouse's mastery of pilferage waned
Because his precious jewel was stolen.
verses.chinese:
随着财富增多势力会增大,
随着财富耗尽势力就削弱;
听说抢来大自在的宝物后,
鼠贼就失去了盗窃的法术。

verses.english:
Upon those who cultivate virtues, wealth falls like rain,
Even when it is given away.
Wealth can be amassed in the absence of virtue,
But think, who will put it to use?
verses.chinese:
为享用福泽而施舍钱财,
钱财就会像春雨般普降,
然没有福泽却拼命积财,
究竟谁来享用是个疑问。

verses.english:
Noble people may decline for awhile,
But later prosper like the waxing moon.
If coarse people decline just once,
They sputter out like a butter lamp.
verses.chinese:
尽管圣者会惨遭不幸,
就像残月必返会圆满;
卑贱者虽然遭难一次,
就像灯灭难摆脱黑暗。

verses.english:
By extending patience to an enemy,
The wise bring them under their influence.
By responding to an enemy's challenge,
The inexperienced meet continuous difficulties.
verses.chinese:
智者对敌也慈悲为怀,
因此将强敌轻易制服;
愚者因时常谋算报复,
困难也就会接连不断。

verses.english:
When the wise avoid dangerous situations,
It is an indication of courage.
When the lion is out to slay a bull,
Would avoiding the horns be cowardly?
verses.chinese:
智者避开险恶的境地,
那样才显出英雄本色,
狮子欲杀水牛的时候,
避开犄角才显露胆略。

verses.english:
Leaping at foes impetuously
Is the telltale sign of a fool.
By fighting with the butter lamp
Does a fly become a hero?
verses.chinese:
在没有查明敌情的时候,
若盲目冲杀是愚者特性;
如扑打油灯而亡的飞蛾,
难道有人将它算作英雄?

verses.english:
Evil people oppress those who depend on them,
But noble people protect those who depend on them.
The silkworm eats away the leaf that bears it,
But the lion protects the land and its inhabitants.
verses.chinese:
恶徒会毁灭自己的依靠,
圣者会保护自己的同伴;
寄生虫吃净自己的资源,
狮子会保护自己的领地。

verses.english:
Coarse people conceal insignificant things,
Yet divulge important secrets for no reason at all.
Noble people do not contrive secrets pointlessly,
Yet guard confidential matters with their lives.
verses.chinese:
卑劣的人喜欢隐瞒小事,
密谋的事却会到处乱讲;
高尚的人不会隐瞒小事,
密谋的事至死不会出口。

恶人变富就会肆无忌惮,
圣人富有更加和和气气,
狐狸吃饱会兴奋得昏死,
狮子吃饱了就安然入睡。

verses.english:
The behavior of both noble and coarse people
Acquires strength through habituation.
Why bother to train a bee to seek flowers,
Or a duck to enter the water?
verses.chinese:
圣者和贱人的所作所为,
都是在习惯中积累而成;
正如蜜蜂采蜜鸭子游泳,
都是不教自会本能一样。

verses.english:
When evil kings confront an enemy
They end up punishing their own subjects.
Some fools who fail in their objectives
Commit suicide by hanging themselves.
verses.chinese:
若暴躁的君王遇见强敌,
用惩罚属民来假装强大;
把事情办砸的无能之臣,
定会有自我毁灭的末日。

verses.english:
When Dharma kings encounter an enemy,
They become even kinder to their subjects.
A mother feels special concern
Toward a child stricken with illness.
verses.chinese:
法王遇到强大的敌人,
倍加爱护自己的臣民;
好像病魔摧残的孩子,
母亲对他会特别慈悲。

verses.english:
Noble people can become very degenerate
When in the company of bad people.
The gratifying water of the Ganges
Becomes saltwater when it reaches the ocean.
verses.chinese:
如果时常亲近卑鄙者,
圣者也会沾染些毛病
尽管恒河水特别甘甜,
流进大海会变成卤水。

verses.english:
When bad people are close to good people,
They assimilate their excellent behavior.
Notice how those daubed with musk scent
Become very fragrant.
verses.chinese:
如果经常向智者讨教,
恶人也习惯高尚行为;
如果在身上涂抹麝香,
自然也会散发出香味。

verses.english:
Like a mountain that absolutely nothing can move,
Extraordinary people maintain consummate stability.
Like small wisps of cotton wafting about,
Coarse people behave unduly erratically.
verses.chinese:
正大山峰岿然不动,
圣人有他坚定信念;
也如柳絮随风飘荡,
贱人永远变化无常。

title.english: Chapter 5 - An Examination of Bad Conduct

verses.english:
The sweet talk of deceitful people
Is due to self-interest, not respect.
The pleasant, laughing cry of the owl
Is an evil omen, not a sign of happiness.
verses.chinese:
狡诈者讲出动听的语言,
均为了私利并非是恭敬;
猫头鹰表示欢心的时候,
正是在散布不祥的预兆。

verses.english:
Bad people first mislead others with their words,
And if that goes well they later swindle them.
Notice how fishermen catch and kill fish
By baiting their hooks with food.
verses.chinese:
恶劣者先用赞美来蒙哄,
放松了警惕就实施骗局;
如渔翁首先要安放香饵,
然后就诱杀无数的鱼鳖。

verses.english:
As long as coarse people remain helpless
They maintain a good disposition.
As long as the poisonous thorn is immature
It cannot prick others.
verses.chinese:
恶者还未变成强大时,
会表现某些善良本性;
如荆棘的毒刺成熟前,
它还是不可能刺伤人。

verses.english:
Some people keep one idea in their minds,
But convey something else with their words.
They are known as "deceivers,"
Fools pretending to be wise.

When deception is carried too far,
It may work for awhile but later brings downfall.
The donkey wearing a leopard skin
Ate the crops, but later was killed.
verses.chinese:
如果过分地玩弄伎俩,
暂成事情终究会败落;
披豹皮偷食禾苗的驴,
最终只有被杀的结局。

verses.english:
If one is wise, one is able
To deceive others with blatant lies.
Because the thieves called it a dog,
The Brahmin boy lost his goat.
verses.chinese:
如果有高超的智慧和胆量,
就能用谎言公开欺骗对方,
如小偷把山羊硬说成是狗,
婆罗门也就只能无可奈何。

verses.english:
Even while indulging in harmful deeds,
Manipulative people deceive others with words.
Mahadeva, while crying out helplessly,
Proclaimed the truth of suffering.
verses.chinese:
正如明目张胆地做恶事,
狡诈者会用美言来行骗;
大梵天失口发出的哀叹,
却又被说成是宣讲苦谛。

verses.english:
Deceivers, well-mannered and smooth talking,
Should not be trusted until scrutinized.
Peacocks have lovely forms and pleasing calls,
But their food is extremely poisonous.
verses.chinese:
骗子们假装慈悲的美言,
在彻底了解前不可信任;
孔雀尽管体美声音也亮,
可它习惯用毒食来充饥。

verses.english:
Deceitful people first put on a good front,
Then later cheat to achieve their objectives.
By exhibiting the tail of a deer,
One shameless fellow sold his donkey meat.
verses.chinese:
若狡诈者伪装成老实人,
那就会是存心要欺骗人;
他们把贵重兽尾示给人,
却无耻地贩卖着毛驴肉。

verses.english:
People of little shame use others' wealth
To show off how important they are.
By displaying a friend's garments for visitors,
They demonstrate their own status.
verses.chinese:
很多寡廉鲜耻的小人们,
会用别人的财物做人情;
把朋友的衣服叠成坐垫,
以此假装对宾客的尊敬。

verses.english:
Because of abysmal degeneracy,
The shameless boast of their own wrongdoing.
In some royal families of the land of Kanci
The royal drum is beaten when the father is slain.
verses.chinese:
很多极端下贱的人,
把丑事炫耀成荣耀;
根泽地方的王族们,
会擂鼓庆祝弑父者。

verses.english:
Sometimes help from the weak-minded
Can be extremely harmful.
The magpie chick plucks out its mother's feathers
Thinking it is expressing gratitude.
verses.chinese:
见识小的人所干的好事,
有候会变成灾难的根源;
雏鹊们拔掉母鹊的羽毛,
还以为报答了养育之恩。

verses.english:
Brazen people think what comes from others' kindness
Is entirely due to their own importance.
Farmers believe themselves magnificent
When the rain falls due to the nagas efforts.
verses.chinese:
别人的恩惠中得到好处,
卑鄙者却炫耀自己有福;
神龙们使劲降下的雨水,
农夫会称是自己的福分。

verses.english:
Conceited people think the benefits of karma
Are due to their own efforts.
Thinking blood from its own punctured palate
To be the bone's marrow, the dog keeps chewing.
verses.chinese:
愚蠢者尽管靠运气生活,
却以为自己努力有结果;
啃骨头刺破上颚的鲜血,
蠢狗却当作骨髓来吸嚼。

verses.english:
The ignorant are seen to destroy their allies
And then take good care of strangers.
Docking a peacock's head tuft to grace its tail is ludicrous;
Who but a madman would do such a thing?
verses.chinese:
愚蠢者抢劫亲人的财产,
去供养和自己无关的人;
把头颅斩下来装饰尾巴,
那就是疯子才干的事情。

verses.english:
Fools do not contribute where there is need,
But are very generous where there is none.
A poor spring flows in summer,
But is dry in springtime when needed most.
verses.chinese:
愚蠢者不会到需要的地方,
不需要的地方却常来常往;
无用的泉水夏季水流成灾,
在春天需要水时却会干枯。

verses.english:
Bad people are especially harmful
Toward peaceful, good people.
The tree trunk that produces resin
Catches fire, while others do not.
verses.chinese:
对于既善良又贤惠的人,
恶人时常既欺凌又诽谤;
那些含油脂最多的灯芯,
必定是火焰专攻的对象。

verses.english:
Failing to rule according to the Dharma
Is the sign of a declining king.
When the sun fails to dispel the darkness.
It is the sign of a solar eclipse.
verses.chinese:
国王需要依法治理国家,
否则他的政权就会衰败;
如果太阳不能驱除黑暗,
定然是已被罗睺星衔食。

verses.english:
A despot who has been appointed ruler,
A house with a damaged top floor,
And a mountain crest that is very unstable -
Living under such conditions is always fearsome.
verses.chinese:
恶人被当选为国王,
及住在快塌的楼下,
和行在将崩的山下,
都会需要提心胆吊。

verses.english:
Somebody may be knowledgeable,
But avoid him if his character is bad.
A poisonous snake may be crowned with a jewel,
But what wise person would place it in his lap?
verses.chinese:
即便有些聪明才智,
品质恶劣仍会抛弃;
尽管蛇头用宝装饰,
智者不会揣在怀里。

verses.english:
Obeying ambitious rulers is difficult,
Disobeying usually makes them unkind,
And doing neither is risky
Some rulers are like raging fires.
verses.chinese:
高傲的国王很难亲近,
疏远了就被彻底忘记,
保持中立就需要担心,
有些国王像烈火一样。

verses.english:
Who would depend on a bad spouse,
A bad friend, or a bad king?
Would sensible people continuously live
In a thick forest of dangerous carnivores?
verses.chinese:
对于卑鄙的妻友和暴君,
不可能有人敢亲近他们;
正如猛兽横行的森林中,
智者不可能会安身一样。

verses.english:
Good personal qualities are ruined by pride;
One's sense of shame is ruined by desire.
When he always criticizes his subjects,
The ruler has gone to ruin.
verses.chinese:
骄傲促使智慧衰落,
贪欲变得寡廉鲜耻,
如果常常欺凌下属,
官高也会身败名裂。

verses.english:
Rare are those who say helpful things;
Rarer still are those who listen.
Skillful doctors are hard to find,
But fewer are those who heed their advice.
verses.chinese:
用善心劝告的特别少,
能听进劝告的更稀少;
有高超医术的很难找,
能遵行医嘱的更少有。

verses.english:
When one is very arrogant,
One is continuously beset with misery.
Due to the lion's great conceit,
The fox induced him to carry the load.
verses.chinese:
假若过分自以为是,
磨难就会接二连三,
因为狮子过分傲慢,
就成了狐狸的脚夫。

verses.english:
Things hidden by crows,
Assistance given to bad people,
And seeds planted in bad fields
Represent lots of hope but are of little use.
verses.chinese:
乌鸦所埋藏的食物,
和为坏人谋求福利,
如荒漠中播撒种子,
均期望多却受益少。

verses.english:
Until someone has been carefully examined,
They should not be trusted nor spoken to candidly.
From carelessness arises trouble;
Conversation often creates enemies.
verses.chinese:
没有详细了解别人前,
不要随便信赖并托事,
随便信人会出大差错,
信口开河就会结怨恨。

verses.english:
Though there are many fearsome things in the world,
Nothing is worse than evil people.
Other bad things can be remedied,
But trying to reform evil people just worsens them.
verses.chinese:
世界上虽有很多逆心事,
但很少像坏人那样可怕,
其他逆心的可以被改造,
但改造坏人会引来麻烦。

verses.english:
One can never satisfy evil people
Even by helping them in a hundred excellent ways.
They become hostile when someone serves them:
This is their special characteristic.
verses.chinese:
即使做尽人间所有善事,
恶者仍然不可能来答谢;
把自己的依靠视为敌人,
这就是恶人的潜在特征。

verses.english:
Try as one might to reform bad people,
They simply do not become good-natured.
Even if one vigorously washes coal,
It simply cannot be made white.
verses.chinese:
无论怎样改造坏人,
本性永远不会变好;
无论怎样洗涤煤炭
永远无法变成白色。

verses.english:
In places dominated by evil people,
Even if sages are seen they are shunned.
In places where harm is inflicted by snakes,
People flee even from golden chains.
verses.chinese:
遭受恶人暗算的地方,
遇见好人也会遭嫌弃,
就在毒蛇咬伤的地方,
遇见金链也要会躲避。

应该供奉的只能是圣人,
如果供奉了恶人要遭灾;
对于人类乳汁就是甘露,
若喂了毒蛇会增长毒液。

verses.english:
However hard they try to acquire it,
Evil people can hardly assimilate kindness.
No matter how hard one tries to remedy death,
It is impossible to remain fearless.
verses.chinese:
尽管真心和他交往,
恶人不会成为知己,
不管怎样喂养麻雀,
也不可能变成温顺。

verses.english:
Those always seeking to instigate disunity
Will split apart even the closest of friends.
When continuously worn away by water,
Will cracks not occur even in rock?
verses.chinese:
喜欢经常制造分歧者,
会使贴心朋友也离走;
正如不断由激流冲刷,
岩石自然也会裂出缝。

verses.english:
Some say they have deceived and acted wrongly
And relate the faults of abbots, teachers, and friends.
When false, such liars cannot be trusted;
When truthful, they arouse apprehension.
verses.chinese:
为了谋私拨弄是非,
又常揭露师友之短,
如果有假不必相信,
如果是真就要防范。

verses.english:
Who would mention in the presence of others
Matters that should remain private?
Whether such things are true or false,
Beware of people so adroit.
verses.chinese:
对于不该谈论秘密者,
如果有人和他要攀谈,
不管谈的是假还是真,
智者必须对他要警惕。

verses.english:
Untrustworthy people greedy for wealth,
Even when friends, should not be trusted;
Taking bribes from friends,
Many powerful people are ruined.
verses.chinese:
恶人总把钱财当命根,
即使亲友也能够变心;
如果伟人受贿遭了灾,
多半是因亲友所造成。

verses.english:
It is easy to destroy enemies
Who clearly show signs of malevolence.
But how is one to overcome enemies
Who give false signs of being helpful?
verses.chinese:
常常把害人挂在嘴边,
这种敌人很容易征服;
言谈尽是利人的誓言,
这种敌人却很难征服。

verses.english:
Some words spoken skillfully can be valid,
But obnoxious words cannot succeed.
Because the crow once humiliated the owl
They have remained antagonistic for eons.
verses.chinese:
其他伤痕可以治疗,
恶语创伤难以全愈;
乌鸦对枭鸟的伤痕,
就会伴随世世代代。

verses.english:
"Hold malice firmly in your heart,
But outwardly speak pleasant words."
This is the advice of evil masters;
It contradicts the ways of noble people.
verses.chinese:
在内心要牢牢记住仇恨,
在嘴里要常常挂些美言。
虽然是恶道隐士的教诲,
却有违圣人贤者的道义。

verses.english:
"Just as one unearths the roots of poisonous plants,
One should sunder enemies at their roots."
Though this appears in the Rajanitishastra,
Enemies act like sons when treated like sons.
verses.chinese:
就想清除毒根一样,•
除敌也要连根拔除。
此话虽然出自《王典》,
若对敌如子回敬如父。

verses.english:
Who could befriend those people
That act only in self-interest?
In fields where one works hard growing crops
There is little chance for other gardening.
verses.chinese:
只知道自私自利的人,
谁还敢跟他结交朋友;
农夫辛勤耕耘的田野,
没有杂草成熟的机会。

verses.english:
How could one ever befriend
Ungracious individuals?
What farmer would cultivate fields
Where even hard work isn't fruitful?
verses.chinese:
对于忘恩负义的恶人,
没有敢交朋友的好人;
辛劳化为泡沫的田里,
不会有农夫反复耕作。

verses.english:
On account of their deceptive behavior
The impetuous quickly deteriorate.
Does the obstinate wild ox
Not quickly break its tether?
verses.chinese:
靠蛮横无理行事的,
恶人会迅速遭衰败;
无所顾忌的溅牯牛,
很快就有人会阉割。

verses.english:
No matter how much one gives to the coarse,
What do they repay when oneself has needs?
A pincer always seizes other things,
But can a round, iron ball grip in return?
verses.chinese:
不管给恶人布施多少,
不可能会有点滴回报;
用钳子经常来夹铁球,
却不会有铁球夹钳子。

verses.english:
Pretentiously claiming, "I will help others"
Bad people engage in wrongdoing.
What wise person would destroy herself
Doing what merely seems to help others?
verses.chinese:
恶人时常会扬言为别人,
最终干出的只会是罪孽;
假托大兴善事来造罪孽,
智者不会用它来毁自己。

verses.english:
Unsettled debt, the root of enmity,
Bad statutes, bad language,
A bad lineage, and bad conduct -
Though unintended, these things naturally worsen.
verses.chinese:
余债和残存的敌人,
苦刑和恶毒的语言,
底下人种和坏习惯,
不被倡导也会泛滥。

title.english: Chapter 6 - An Examination of Natural Tendencies

verses.english:
When named to a high position,
One rarely knows what to do.
Though one has eyes to see others,
A mirror is required to see oneself.
verses.chinese:
如果自己被派去做官,
很少能知道如何去办;
不仅需要观人的眼睛,
特别需要查己的镜子。

verses.english:
Those who have one-sided wisdom
Find it hard to be skillful in everything.
Although the eyes see very clearly,
They are incapable of hearing sound.
verses.chinese:
尽管在某一方造诣高深,
不可能精通人间所有事;
尽管是非常敏锐的眼睛,
也不可捕取美妙的音乐。

verses.english:
It is possible for honest speech to be faulty
And for dishonest speech to be constructive.
Some direct routes can ruin one's wealth,
While the white conch shell twists to the right.
verses.chinese:
有时说实话也会出漏子,
有时拐弯子也能有用处;
笔直的路上可能遭劫持,
右旋的海螺能引来吉祥。

verses.english:
People with some learning but no merit
Destroy themselves with their knowledge.
Oysters forfeit their lives
Because of the pearls to which they cling.
verses.chinese:
如果没有宏大福泽,
知识也会引来灾难;
有些蚌壳藏有珍珠,
结果就把性命送掉。

verses.english:
When too dependent on someone, even if learned,
It is frequently possible to have regrets.
Even though sugar cane is tasty,
When always served, it is often refused.
verses.chinese:
尽管是个有智慧的学者,
过分依靠就免不了烦恼,
尽管甘蔗有甘甜的味道,
经常吃了也免不了厌弃。

verses.english:
Even those who are good-natured
Will grow malicious when continually abused.
Though sandalwood sticks are cool by nature,
When rubbed together they burst into flames.
verses.chinese:
尽管是性情善良的人,
不断折磨也会要报复;
尽管檀香是清凉物种,
不断磨擦也能会燃烧。

verses.english:
Although rulers are quite numerous,
Only a few govern according to the Dharma.
Although heavenly abodes of the gods are many,
None shines as brightly as the sun and the moon.
verses.chinese:
虽然天下有很多国王,
奉法爱民的特别少见;
虽然天上有很多神仙,
日月同辉者特别稀有。

verses.english:
Anyone with the power to be harmful
Is also able to be helpful.
A king with the power to cut off one's head
Is also able to govern justly.
verses.chinese:
敢于制造事端的人,
也是能办好事的人;
敢砍别人脑袋的人,
也能把江山赠别人。

verses.english:
The high official who is honest and intelligent
Achieves all objectives of the king and the people.
When a straight arrow is skillfully shot,
Whatever is aimed at is hit.
verses.chinese:
如果是智慧正直的大臣,
既能成君愿又能顺民意;
如果是神箭手射出的箭,
不管瞄上什么都能射中。

verses.english:
When the king himself is disrespectful,
Not even the omniscient will honor him.
Even if a lifeless human corpse is attractive,
Who would want such a thing?
verses.chinese:
如果国王不会尊重自己,
尽管是全知也无人尊敬,
如果是没有生命的尸体,
尽管再贤良也没人恭维。

verses.english:
When many are of the same opinion,
Even the weak can achieve great things.
Through the united force of many ants
A lion cub was slain, it is said.
verses.chinese:
只要众人齐心协力,
弱者也能办成大事;
据说结成群的蚂蚁,
夺取了幼狮的性命。

verses.english:
Timid people who shun spirited effort
Will deteriorate even if they are strong.
Although the elephant is very powerful,
It is enslaved by a slender mahout.
verses.chinese:
胆小怕事又不愿恩赐者,
尽管强大也会很快衰败;
大象虽然显得强大无比,
却成了牧童温顺的坐骑。

verses.english:
When one generates self-confidence and enthusiasm,
One one's brilliance intimidates even the great.
Although the white conch is small,
It is the great crocodile's executioner.
verses.chinese:
自信而能付艰辛的人,
遇到强者也能够制服;
海螺虽只有微小躯体,
却成了鲸鱼的夺命者。

verses.english:
The great need not be arrogant;
For coarse people, what is the use?
Precious gems need no advertising,
But who would purchase trinkets?
verses.chinese:
伟人根本用不着骄傲,
小人的骄傲成不了事;
若是真宝用不着赞美,
岩石再夸也没有用处。

verses.english:
The wealth of the truly great endures,
That of the coarse is at risk.
The sun endlessly radiates light,
But the moon waxes, then wanes.
verses.chinese:
圣人的财富能够长久,
恶人的钱财时临衰败;
太阳永远能光辉灿烂,
月亮下玄时开始衰败。

verses.english:
Excessive praise of an evil king's status
Eventually will lead to his destruction.
When an egg is thrown up into the sky,
What else can happen than for it to break?
verses.chinese:
若王者过分炫耀权势,
最后只能会土崩瓦解;
如果将鸡蛋扔向高空,
也只能有摔碎的结果。

verses.english:
As a rule, people are harmed
By others of their own kind.
When sun rays begin to dawn
Other light sources vanish.
verses.chinese:
如果说有人惨遭陷害,
按惯例应是同类所为;
每当太阳升起的时候,
星星会变得无踪无影。

若有益对敌也应接近,
若有害是亲也该放弃;
海中宝物虽远也应买,
腹中疼痛虽近更该治。

verses.english:
With the inner thought, "I'm rather rich,"
An outward expression of smugness is shown.
When clouds are completely laden with moisture,
They swirl and roll with thunder.
verses.chinese:
如果获得点滴学问,
就会露出傲慢神情;
正如乌云集满了水,
常常就要翻滚打雷。

verses.english:
Those with all good qualities are rare,
So also those with none at all.
Rather than a mix of good and bad,
The wise mainly rely on good qualities.
verses.chinese:
像具备所有优点的一样,
没有优点的也不会存在;
优点和缺点集于一身时,
聪明人往往更喜欢优点。

verses.english:
At the outset one is uncertain
Who is a friend, who is an enemy.
Undigested food turns into poison,
But even poison cures if understood.
verses.chinese:
敌人和朋友的区分,
不可能是生来便在;
食物不消化成毒素,
识别了毒性变良药。

verses.english:
Those with favorable karma are rich;
Those lacking such karma are poor.
Ducks, though put in a house, do not stay there,
Though flushed from a lake, they circle and return.
verses.chinese:
有因缘的地方会兴旺,
无因缘的地方要衰败;
野鸭养在家里会飞走,
从湖面上却无法驱散。

verses.english:
The wise will pay to better their knowledge,
But fools discard what they've already learned.
Most people take medicine when sick,
But some commit suicide when healthy.
verses.chinese:
聪明人化钱求知识,
愚蠢人赐教也放弃,
智者有病拿药治疗,
愚者没病也会寻死。

自由会成幸福的源泉,
限制只能会带来痛苦;
两者兼顾会带来分歧,
固守己见会变为死结。

verses.english:
One who internally has all good qualities
Yet is outwardly unkempt is scorned by all.
It is said that even though bats are wise,
Their baldness makes all birds spurn them.
verses.chinese:
尽管是满腹经纶者,
离经叛道会遭人欺;
蝙蝠虽然有好本事,
因没有羽毛被鸟弃。

verses.english:
When unsuitable people speak too honestly,
They destroy themselves and others.
An arrow will either kill someone
Or will itself be destroyed.
verses.chinese:
不合理性地憨直行事,
既毁自己也会害他人;
尽管弓箭能射死敌人,
同样也会把自己撞折。

verses.english:
Rain and rivers flow to the ocean;
Intelligence and knowledge adhere to the wise.
Wealth and subjects are gathered by the king,
Forests grow in warm, damp places.
verses.chinese:
雨水和河水会流向大海,
聪明和智慧会选择智者,
财富和臣民会集在王府,
肥沃并温湿处生长丛林。

verses.english:
Springs that flow in summer, fires of grass,
The sun or full moon peeking between the clouds,
Friends with poor knowledge and low intelligence:
At the time of need, their appearance is uncertain.
verses.chinese:
夏天的泉水和燃草的火,
云罩的太阳和圆满的月,
愚者的智慧和结交卑友,
需要之时却不一定会有。

愚蠢的奴才应保持沉默,
聪慧的王者应深居简出,
能偶尔观赏魔术才新奇,
罕见的珍宝方才显珍贵。

verses.english:
When love,is lavished excessively,
That in itself generates hostility.
Most of the disputes in the world
Derive from close relationships.
verses.chinese:
如果过分地以慈悲相待,
慈悲也变成仇恨的种子;
人间所有的矛盾和怨恨,
都是起源于微妙的关系。

verses.english:
It is possible for heated arguments
To result in close friendships.
Usually following controversy
Reconciliation is observed.
verses.chinese:
对于智者来讲激烈的争论,
也能成为促进友好的因素,
人们常常经过激烈的争论,
最终和解而终者比比皆是。

verses.english:
The wealth of the greedy,
The friends of the jealous,
The lore of evil minds:
These exist, but cannot bring joy.
verses.chinese:
吝啬鬼所拥有的财宝,
嫉妒者所表现的友好,
庸人们能讲述的道理,
绝不可能会带来欣慰。

贪得无厌者喜欢钱财,
骄傲自大者爱听夸奖,
愚昧无知者爱以类集,
贤惠善良者爱讲真话。

verses.english:
The qualities of coarse people,
The knowledge of weak braggarts,
And the gratitude of evil rulers:
The chance that these will benefit others is slim.
verses.chinese:
恶人拥有的学识,
懦夫拥有的才智,
暴君赐与的恩惠,
都难以成就效果。

verses.english:
What a wealthy person says is considered charming,
But the words of the poor are rejected, even when true.
Even wood from ordinary trees is quite costly
When it comes from the land of white sandalwood.
verses.chinese:
有财者的话语常常有分量,
无财者讲真话也没人倾听,
只要货物的产源是玛拉雅,
尽管是一节朽木照样很贵。

话语多了会招来灾祸,
沉默寡言是免灾之本;
鹦鹉学舌会关进笼子,
鲁钝飞禽能自由翱翔。

verses.english:
Whenever anyone in an undeceitful way
Gives assistance to an enemy,
And the enemy is straightforward in return,
Such mutual respect is true greatness.
verses.chinese:
如果对敌人不欺不诈,
并能时常制造些利益,
敌人也能会以诚相待,
此乃走向和谐的法宝。

verses.english:
What use is there for the weak to get angry?
What need is there for the strong to get angry?
Therefore, no matter what one is doing,
Pointless anger is a self-consuming fire.
verses.chinese:
弱小者愤怒没有用处,
强大者没有必要愤怒:
为了办事而引起愤怒,
只能成为无奈的自焚。

verses.english:
Even foes gather for charity,
But without it, even friends stay away.
When the cow's milk has dried up,
Though restrained, the calf tries to flee.
verses.chinese:
若能施舍敌人也会投奔,
无所施舍亲人也会离开;
母牛的乳汁干枯的时候,
尽管圈住牛犊也会跑掉。

verses.english:
Just because one is skilled in some areas
Does not mean they can do other things.
The swan, which can separate milk from water,
Imagines some things it sees to be food.
verses.chinese:
只精通某些事情的人,
不能肯定精通其他事;
野鸭能从水中分乳汁,
却会把影子当成猎物。

verses.english:
When leaders always treat people kindly,
It is easy for them to find followers.
Ducks need not be called to lotus ponds;
But gather there naturally.
verses.chinese:
用恩典来保护奴仆的,
仁慈使主人易找奴仆;
盛产着莲花的湖水中,
常会有嬉水的天鹅群。

verses.english:
Proper use of wealth by the rich,
Self-discipline after becoming learned,
And good care of the lowly by the great -
These three bring joy to others and help oneself.
verses.chinese:
富有钱财者广施恩惠,
满腹经纶者温文尔雅,
伟大的能够爱护下属:
三者既利人又能利己。

verses.english:
Things achieved through the strength of merit,
Like the light of the sun, depend on nothing else.
Things achieved through the strength of effort,
Like the light of a butter lamp, depend on everything else.
verses.chinese:
依靠福泽来成就事业者,
正如太阳有自身的光芒;
依靠勤奋来成就事业者,
如同油灯需要依靠外力。

verses.english:
When they rely on the great,
Even the lowly achieve greatness.
See how a vine that clings to a tall tree
Climbs all the way to the top.
verses.chinese:
如果是紧紧依靠伟人,
恶人也能够变得温顺;
正如青藤依靠着大树,
就能够爬到树顶一样。

verses.english:
Those who admire good qualities should depend on others
Who, though having faults, possess good qualities.
Rain can damage a manor house,
But it makes the farmers very pleased.
verses.chinese:
虽然学者也有毛病,
爱学问的仍会亲近;
雨水虽对房屋有害,
可人们还是喜爱它。

verses.english:
If people simply look nice but lack good qualities,
The wise cannot take any interest in them.
If a champion horse lacks a good gait,
Even if good tempered, it is of little value.
verses.chinese:
不学无术而只凭打扮,
不能得到智者的欢喜;
骏马没有奔跑的脚力,
非常温顺也没有价值。

愚蠢的人中也有富翁,
勇敢者常在兽群现身,
格言常被智者们吟诵,
绝世圣人最难以遇见。

verses.english:
Whatever qualities people possess
Are those by which they gain their reputation.
Wisdom establishes the reputation of the wise,
And bravery is how heroes acquire their fame.
verses.chinese:
个人有什么样的本领,
就有相应的名声荣耀,
智者以学识闻名于世,
英雄以勇猛无敌出众。

verses.english:
Those honored by the great
Are scorned by the coarse.
The moon ornament on mighty Shiva's head
Is devoured by lesser gods.
verses.chinese:
被伟大的供养的事物,
会遭到卑贱者的糟蹋;
如天神大自在的头饰,
阿修罗会当食物侵吞。

verses.english:
Knowledge left behind in books,
Tantric practices unaccomplished,
Instructions completely forgotten:
These often deceive in times of need.
verses.chinese:
存在于经卷中的学问,
还未修成正果的密乘,
健忘的人所学的知识,
需要的时候却又误事。

verses.english:
Even though wealthy, if the intelligent are lazy
It is hard for them to gain high position.
Though ears emerge first at the time of birth,
Are the horns not seen to be more prominent?
verses.chinese:
智者能随时发家致富,
懒汉却永远难以富裕,
真如耳朵虽然长在先,
后长的犄角就比它高。

verses.english:
Gourmet food for dogs and pigs,
Butter lamps for the blind,
A meal for those with indigestion,
And Dharma for fools - of what use are these?
verses.chinese:
猪狗之辈用不着味香,
盲人同样不需要明灯,
消化不良者厌恶食物,
愚者同样会远离佛法。

verses.english:
Fine gold, knowledgeable people,
Heroic warriors, champion horses,
Skillful doctors, and beautiful jewelry
Wherever one goes these are in demand.
verses.chinese:
学识渊博者和黄金,
英勇无敌者和骏马,
医术高超者和盛装,
到处都能受到欢迎。

verses.english:
As for the intelligent and hard-working ones,
Of course they can achieve their goals!
It is said that the sons of King Pandu
Conquered twelve divisions of the king of Kaurava.
verses.chinese:
既聪明又能勤奋的人,
什么事都能顺利完成;
俱卢十二部族的兵马,
就是被班图五子所灭。

verses.english:
Usually the conduct of children
Follows in line with their ancestry.
There is no way for a cuckoo chick
To mature into a sparrow hawk.
verses.chinese:
儿孙们的所作所为,
大部分传承于父辈;
小杜鹃虽有大变化,
却不可能变成鹞子。

verses.english:
Mountains and rivers, elephants and horses,
Wood and light, jewels and stones,
Men and women - though each is a unique type,
There are qualitative variations in each.
verses.chinese:
对于山和水及大象和马,
柴和火以及宝石和岩石,
男子汉和妇女等等来说,
虽然同类却有优劣之分。

verses.english:
The lowly endure with difficulty
Even mere words from virtuous people.
The ocean king was bound, it is said,
By mere words from the king of Gauda.
verses.chinese:
尽管是有福者的一句话,
对于弱者也可望尘莫及;
正如果摘国王的一句话,
就把大海之王束手就擒。

verses.english:
One may vigorously strive to complete a task,
But attainments depend on the power of virtue.
A jewel that merchants cannot find in the ocean
Is possessed in the treasure house of the king.
verses.chinese:
虽然办理事情非常努力,
如果想要成功得靠福分;
商人在大海获得的宝物,
却储存在国王的宝库中。

verses.english:
Signs of love and anger in fools are recognizable,
But in those with guile they can appear differently.
When dogs bare their fangs, it is a sign they will bite;
When the Lord of Death smiles, it is a sign he will kill.
verses.chinese:
愚者的爱憎从表情看出,
智者的爱憎却恰恰相反:
恶狗表示友好时要咬人,
阎王微笑时就会夺人命。

施舍是最佳的宝物,
慈悲是最大的快乐,
智慧是最美的装饰,
诚实是最好的朋友。

verses.english:
Who is there with no worries about wealth?
Who can sit comfortably all the time?
All suffering and happiness change,
Just as summer turns into winter.
verses.chinese:
没有人不为钱财所苦,
也没人永远享受幸福,
就在幸福和痛苦之间,
也会有冬夏般的循环。

verses.english:
Merely by dropping the names of the great,
The lowly are protected by others.
It is taught that by using Angulimala's name
One is protected from common misleaders.
verses.chinese:
如果弱小者能有好声誉,
全部来自靠别人的保护;
如嗜杀成性的魔鬼指蔓,
就需要毗那夜迦的保护。

verses.english:
Any relationship between sentient beings
Takes shape in accord with past karma.
Notice vultures with marmots on their backs
And otters making offerings to owls.
verses.chinese:
在众生中谁与谁有缘,
都由前世的命运决定,
正如大鹰要背负哈拉,
水獭要供猫头鹰一样。

verses.english:
If the rich want to increase their wealth,
Its best insurance is to give it away.
If you want to add more water to a pond,
Draw down the pond and it replenishes itself.
verses.chinese:
如果是个想积攒钱财者,
施舍是最佳的守财办法;
如果想把河水引进池塘,
首先退水才是养池良方。

title.english: Chapter 7 - An Examination of Unseemly Tendencies

verses.english:
Servants who are very arrogant,
Ascetics who behave foppishly,
And kings who act contrary to the Dharma:
These three engage in unseemly conduct.
verses.chinese:
奴仆表现出骄傲自大,
和苦行者爱讲究衣着,
及国王不行正法明道,
都是违背情理的事情。

verses.english:
Starting work that one lacks time to complete,
Being hostile to many, arguing with the powerful,
Trusting shameless spouses, and befriending bad people:
These five are causes for swift self-destruction,
verses.chinese:
从事些难以完成的事情,
同众人结仇并对抗强者,
偏信女人并和恶人结交,
五者是加速自灭的因子。

身无分文却想着华丽服饰,
向行人乞讨却又傲气冲天,
不懂经典又想辩出些真理,
三者都是众人嘲笑的把柄。

verses.english:
Despite the good places to live that exist,
Bad people stay destitute, attached to bad places.
Who but a jackal is going to expect
That the kimsuka flower is a piece of meat?
verses.chinese:
虽然有美丽富饶的地方,
恶人却喜欢在穷乡受苦;
会把郁金花臆想成肉块,
只有恶狼才会有此妄想。

verses.english:
The close associates of important people
Can do them more harm than enemies.
How can the body of a lion be eaten
By any creature other than its own vermin.
verses.chinese:
如果伟大的人惨遭陷害,
其随从比敌人更有可能;
除了身上自生的虱子外,
不可能还有谁敢咬狮子。

verses.english:
When a king inflicts harm on people,
Who is there to defend the king?
When a light casts a shadow on some figure,
There is no way to see it.
verses.chinese:
君王要想伤害他人,
就没有人能敢救护;
如果想要证明幻影,
不可能有观察方法。

verses.english:
For Dharma practitioners living peacefully,
Harmful acts are particularly despicable.
Who can ever consider brave
One who kills those seeking protection?
verses.chinese:
如果会陷害奉公守法者,
肯定是些卑鄙下流的人;
如果杀害自己的救命人,
不可能有人称他为英雄。

verses.english:
Bad individuals inflict harm on others
Even when they derive no benefit from it.
Poisonous snakes strike at the wind as food;
Do they not also kill others when they see food?
verses.chinese:
尽管对自己没有好处,
坏人还是会伤害他人;
毒蛇虽然以气为食物,
但见到生灵仍会咬死。

verses.english:
Although it is believed that desires bring happiness,
Acting on such impulses brings only misery.
Those who think drinking beer is happiness
Assume their intoxication is bliss.
verses.chinese:
尽管有人把贪欲当成幸福,
其实只能加重痛苦的根源;
同样有人把喝酒当成幸福,
其实就把疯狂误认为幸福。

verses.english:
Ordinary people respect those with good qualities;
Much effort is required to obtain them.
What is the point of being arrogant toward others,
Without having perfected one's own good qualities?
verses.chinese:
智者会受到世人的尊敬,
学问是依靠勤奋的结晶,
不依靠勤奋来积累学问,
抱怨别人没有什么用处。

verses.english:
See how people pray for long life,
Yet are fearful of growing old.
Not wanting to age yet wanting longevity
Is the perverse notion of a fool.
verses.chinese:
人们会羡慕长寿者,
并认为衰老是灾难,
又怕衰老又想长寿,
只能是愚人的邪念。

verses.english:
At times when wise people are available,
Those who learn nothing from them
Are either affected by demons
Or suffering the influence of past karma.
verses.chinese:
当学者仍然健在的时候,
不愿意向他求取知识者,
不是被魔鬼缠住了身心,
就是遭到了厄运的折腾。

verses.english:
When those who happen to have some wealth
Fail to use it or give it away,
Either they are stricken with disease
Or are appearing as pretas.
verses.chinese:
如果拥有大量的钱财时,
既不动用又不乐于施舍,
这种人可能被病魔缠身,
或者是个活生生的饿鬼。

verses.english:
If Dharma is understood but not practiced,
How could it be of any use?
A harvest may be bountiful
But would that delight a carnivore?
verses.chinese:
懂得教义却不愿意奉行,
这种教义没有什么用处;
尽管庄稼长得特别茁壮,
可是对野兽就没有诱惑。

verses.english:
Those who suffer the effects of bad karma
Cannot enjoy wealth even if they have it.
Though the crow may be hungry, it hides its food.
How then can it possibly fill its belly?
verses.chinese:
受到命运所折腾的众生,
尽管有财富也无法享用;
乌鸦饿着肚子也会埋食,
但自己忍着饥饿的痛苦。

verses.english:
If wealth neither enjoyed nor given away
Prompt thoughts of being well off,
Then imagining a mountain to be gold
Would be an easy way to get rich.
verses.chinese:
把既不用又不施的财富,
如果认定是富裕的象征;
就像把大山当作是金子,
想变成富裕就非常容易。

verses.english:
Though many are skilled in discussing
What is Dharma and what is not,
Those who practice such understanding
Are extremely rare in this world.
verses.chinese:
尽管在内外教派方面,
能讲出道理的特别多;
能够遵循所知道理的,
力行者反显得特别少。

verses.english:
Though one may have good ancestry, physique, and youth,
Without knowledge one lacks beauty.
Though the peacock's feathers are handsome,
Are they suitable ornaments for the great ones?
verses.chinese:
尽管种姓高贵体貌又端庄,
如果没有学问就不算优秀;
正如孔雀的羽毛虽然美丽,
却不成为伟人的装饰一样。

verses.english:
Imitation noses, purchased children,
Borrowed jewelry, stolen wealth, and
Knowledge gained without spiritual masters
These exist but are not respected by others.
verses.chinese:
嫁接的鼻子及买来的儿子,
借来的服饰和偷来的钱财,
以及没有以师相传的手艺,
尽管拥有也不会得到承认。

verses.english:
Those with no gratitude for kindness
Harm themselves more than others.
People who cast malevolent spells
Suffer the consequences before their enemies do.
verses.chinese:
从来不感恩戴德的人,
对己比对他人更有害;
正如修炼害人密咒者,
害人前首先自我倒霉。

verses.english:
Though one might look forward to becoming wealthy,
Who would take riches from an unsuitable source?
By licking the spilled blood of battling rams,
The fox's head was smashed to pieces.
verses.chinese:
尽管有发财的好机会,
不合时宜会带来恶果;
公羊相碰头流出的血,
狐狸去舔时断送了命。

verses.english:
After ingratiating oneself with some associates,
Do not opportunistically abandon others;
Even Indra and his attendants
Go everywhere together like camphor.
verses.chinese:
因存在种种因缘关系,
不该把别人随意抛弃;
即便是因陀罗大天王,
其属下也会纷纷逃走。

verses.english:
Do not abandon long-standing friendships
And then shift loyalties to new companions.
It is known that by relying on the crow minister
The king of owls destroyed himself.
verses.chinese:
不要轻易地放弃老朋友后,
就急着去依靠新交的朋友;
正如猫头鹰把乌鸦当军师,
就带来了全军覆灭的结果。

verses.english:
One tries hard to depend on bad people,
But they do not become trusted allies.
No matter how much water is boiled,
It cannot possibly burst into flames.
verses.chinese:
对坏人也可以竭力亲近,
想变成自己的人是妄想;
不管用什么方法来煎水,
不可能在水中生出火焰。

verses.english:
Justifiable anger is somewhat acceptable
And can even be quelled,
But who knows how to placate
Anger that lacks tenable cause?
verses.chinese:
如果是弄清事因的愤怒,
既有些道理也能够解决,
如果是无缘无故的愤怒,
任何人也没有办法解决。

verses.english:
Do not abuse even humble enemies,
Without assessing their capacity.
Because the little tadibala bird was mistreated,
The garuda destroyed the entire ocean.
verses.chinese:
没有弄清敌人的详情之前,
表面示弱也不要随便歧视;
由于歧视陀地巴鸟的原因,
海龙殿也会被揭楼罗毁灭。

福泽耗尽时会产生恶念,
家族衰败时会产生孽子,
金钱挥尽时会产生吝啬,
寿元将到时会产生死兆。

verses.english:
If someone does not engage in wrongdoing,
He cannot be criticized, even by Indra.
If a spring has not ceased flowing of its own accord,
How then can it be stopped by covering it with earth?
verses.chinese:
如果自己不做违法事,
因陀罗神也无可奈何;
如泉眼没有自然干涸,
不可能用泥土来填住。

verses.english:
Those who start a hundred different schemes
Are unable to achieve even one success.
These crazy-minded individuals are
Like old dogs always roaming the town.
verses.chinese:
喜欢着手很多的事情,
却不能完成一件事情;
见异思迁的人像恶狗,
常常在村庄间乱串游。

verses.english:
When led by the force of karma,
The intelligent go down the wrong path.
Shiva, the supreme leader of the Tirthikas,
Once behaved like a lunatic.
verses.chinese:
如果受到命运的驱使,
圣哲也可能走向邪路;
因为修行外道的禁戒,
有人进入疯狂的状态。

verses.english:
Howsoever anyone breaks the law,
They may win for awhile, but eventually they lose.
Although Valaka gained the entire world,
Because he violated the law, the Lion killed him.
verses.chinese:
在违背法度的前提下,
暂时获胜者终会败落;
虽海鹅违法得了土地,
最后还是被狮子杀死。

verses.english:
When an excess of intelligence
Makes one too involved, one ruins oneself.
A king with too many ideas
Brings much degradation to the land.
verses.chinese:
尽管拥有很大的智慧,
从事的事多了要毁己;
正如想法很多的国王,
多因费事而失去政权。

verses.english:
The wealth one has accumulated to excess
Becomes one's executioner.
Mostly the rich experience downfall,
While beggars move about happily.
verses.chinese:
过多地积累的钱财,
会成自己的刽子手;
富翁家常出败家子,
然而乞丐反能安泰。

verses.english:
Becoming excessively powerful
Is preparation for one's own suicide.
Death on the battlefield
Often befalls the mighty.
verses.chinese:
如果有过强的武艺,
就会有送命的前兆:
很多丧生在战场的,
多半都出自勇汉中。

verses.english:
Wealth, wisdom, and power
Are aids to those with virtues.
But for anyone lacking virtues,
They all are a cause of ruin.
verses.chinese:
钱财及智慧和权势,
会成有福者的帮手,
对于那些无福的人,
却成为丧命的因子。

verses.english:
No matter what tasks the wise undertake,
They first check their merit, then act.
In troubled times splendid merit is rare,
Even for one person in a hundred.
verses.chinese:
无论智者做什么事情,
都要按照其福分行事;
加入争论的众人当中,
很少会出现有福的人。

verses.english:
If a substandard pond is filled with water
One of its embankments will surely collapse.
Likewise, an enduring family line-is rare
For anybody who is rich.
verses.chinese:
想让臭水池灌满水,
必须得有个决口处;
如有人富于钱财时,
家丁兴旺的就很少。

verses.english:
People with children seldom have wealth:
If they do they are ruined by enemies.
When good fortune has been fully achieved,
One usually dies at an early age.
verses.chinese:
子孙满堂者却无横财,
若具备了就会遭敌灭,
如果是样样都齐全者,
此人必定成为短命鬼。

verses.english:
Therefore, the wise accumulate virtues,
The sole precondition for prosperity.
Wherever anybody has good fortune,
That indicates the accrual of virtues.
verses.chinese:
智者都会积累福泽,
唯有福泽才能圆满;
若谁在各方都圆满,
那就是积福的标志。

verses.english:
When one thinks, "I deceived others by lying,"
One really deceives oneself.
The telling of a single falsehood
Prompts mistrust when later one is truthful.
verses.chinese:
如果认为通过用谎言,
骗了别人实际在自欺;
真的有过说谎的经历,
说真话也没有人相信。

verses.english:
One who gets angry and berates others
Without carefully checking what is right or wrong
Is like the pigeon who killed his wife,
Then agonized over the loss of her companionship.
verses.chinese:
如果根本不会仔细分析,
会在愤怒之下就要害人;
就好像杀了妻子的鸽子,
会遭遇失去伴侣的痛苦。

verses.english:
Without overanalyzing the future,
Work hard when the time comes.
Why take off your shoes
Before you reach the river?
verses.chinese:
未来的事情不必过于敏感,
只有遇到时才需寻根问底;
正如遇见河水才需要脱靴,
不到河边时没有人会脱鞋。

verses.english:
One should not start things that, though worthy,
Cannot be completed in the future.
A food may taste delicious,
But if indigestible, who will eat it?
verses.chinese:
如果是不能办完的事,
再好的事也不要开头;
若是不能消化的食物,
再香也没有人会食用。

verses.english:
Sitting around and avoiding hard work,
Nothing is achieved for either this or future lives.
Even though the fields are excellent,
Good harvests are not obtained without effort.
verses.chinese:
如果不肯勤奋却贪图安逸,
今生和来世均不会有成就;
如果不把工夫下在耕耘上,
土地肥沃也不可能有收获。

verses.english:
When too subdued in the wrong situation,
One is taken advantage of by all.
Cotton is used for mattresses;
Who would use sticks for a bed?
verses.chinese:
如果是不合时宜的温顺,
人人都想尽办法来奴役;
正如会用棉花来作垫子,
也不可能用树枝当垫子。

verses.english:
Foolish are those who commit evil deeds,
Attempt the impossible, or request others do so.
Who trusts somebody that buys poisonous potions?
Who can say, "I will give away everything!"?
verses.chinese:
坏事和不能成功的事情,
即按托付去做也是蠢人;
没人会买贩毒者的货物,
谁也不敢说一切能施舍。

verses.english:
Amassing wealth but not putting it to good use
Is like gathering firewood to incinerate oneself.
Bees, when they fail to consume their own honey
And others carry it off, are killing themselves.
verses.chinese:
如果只会积财而不用,
就像积累柴火来自焚;
正如蜜蜂酿蜜却不吃,
被人取走时会送性命。

verses.english:
When bright people perform even minor works,
They always consult others before acting.
Even unfinished tasks bring them dignity,
To say nothing of things they complete.
verses.chinese:
智者尽管办的是小事,
也会通过商量后办理,
如果办成了就是好事,
同样办砸了也很体面。

verses.english:
Because people have different inclinations
It is hard for anyone to please everybody.
But those with good personal qualities
Are most likely to make others happy.
verses.chinese:
众生的欲望无限多样,
没有人能圆众生之愿;
如果自己成就了智者,
就能接近别人的志趣。

verses.english:
Even those who have grown very old
Should continue to improve their knowledge.
The benefit for future lives just from learning
Is even greater than that from charity.
verses.chinese:
尽管年龄十分苍老,
还是需要广学博闻;
对来世有益的闻道,
不可能被施舍替代。

verses.english:
Either rely on those who are fully learned,
Or enjoy the friendship of common folk.
Water jugs that are completely full or
Completely empty are easiest to carry.
verses.chinese:
追随博学多闻的大师,
和结伴平凡者能放心;
正如灌满水的容器和,
没水的容器都易挪动。

verses.english:
Who could place their confidence
In those with but little knowledge?
Who would carry upon their head
A jug only half filled with water?
verses.chinese:
只懂一知半解之徒,
不会有人向他求学;
只装半载水的容器,
不会有人顶在头上。

verses.english:
Knowing how to complete a task
By understanding well the difference
Between noble and coarse individuals
Is the foundation of all good fortune.
verses.chinese:
如果有人能清楚地懂得,
圣愚者之间的细微区别,
并懂得怎样去办理事情,
就有了圆满一切的根本。

verses.english:
When well cared for by the wise,
Even coarse people can achieve excellence.
When trained by one who knows how to teach,
Even a parrot can learn to talk.
verses.chinese:
如果是由智者精心培养,
恶人也能表现高尚行为;
如果是由专家调教训练,
鹦鹉也能够诵经并读典。

verses.english:
Even the lowly and weak will succeed
When they rely on others who are great.
Not even tiny drops of water dry up
When mixed together with the sea.
verses.chinese:
如果能够依靠强大的人,
弱者也能办成一些事情;
尽管水滴显得非常渺少,
汇入大海就能永不干枯。

verses.english:
When one is lacking in understanding,
Question well those of great understanding.
If enemies cannot be killed by hand,
Are weapons not used against them?
verses.chinese:
如果自己没有才智,
应该咨询其他智者;
正如空手不能杀敌,
就会拿起武器一样。

verses.english:
Though enemies are harmful,
If one has skill they can be befriended.
Though strong poison will harm the body,
It can be medicine if correctly prepared.
verses.chinese:
尽管是谋财害命的敌人,
如果有计谋也能成朋友;
剧毒虽对身体特别有害,
懂得调配照样变成良药。

verses.english:
Accept wealth that has been properly acquired,
But do not covet others' things; they should not be taken.
Pick fruit directly from the tree,
But let what has fallen stay on the ground.
verses.chinese:
智慧的财物应该攫取,
贪得的欲望必须除掉;
.树梢上的果子可以摘,
超过了树梢就会掉落。

verses.english:
Misfortune befalls the wise
So long as they fail to persevere.
But when the wise persevere greatly,
The chances for misfortune are slim.
verses.chinese:
如果智者不谨慎行事
就免不了发生些不幸;
如果智者能随时留心,
很难发生不幸的事情。

verses.english:
"While strength is partial respect your foes;
Once you have been fully capable
Take whatever approach works best."
Some treatises offer this advice.
verses.chinese:
自己的力量还没强大之前,
特别需要向敌人表示恭敬,
自身强大时可以随意行事,
以上均出自相关的经典中。

verses.english:
Even when enemies speak sweetly,
The intelligent do not believe them.
Herons, cats, by being stealthy,
Always try to kill other creatures.
verses.chinese:
尽管敌人的言语特别动听,
若是聪明人不会轻易相信;
鱼鹰和狸猫虽然显得柔顺,
但其本能仍然暗藏着杀机。

verses.english:
Even if the ruler of the land is hostile,
One should stay on and graciously serve.
Even if one's leg slips on the ground,
One still needs the ground for support.
verses.chinese:
尽管对地方首领很厌烦,
还是需要对其恭敬相处;
正如尽管会滑倒在地上,
还得依靠大地才能站立。

verses.english:
By being greedy for desirable things,
People quickly destroy themselves.
By being so enticed by meat on a hook,
Fish are instantly killed.
verses.chinese:
被贪婪失魂落魄的人,
很快把自己引向毁灭;
如禁不住钩饵的诱惑,
鱼群纷纷被渔翁诱杀。

verses.english:
Those worthy of honor along with their retinue
Gather followers because they are always generous.
All beings from gods to pretas
Gladly protect those who give tormas.
verses.chinese:
对高贵者和自己的下属,
时常需要用布施来笼络;
对于能布施很多供品者,
从天神到饿鬼都愿保护。

verses.english:
The great rid themselves of attachment
To frivolity, pleasure, and food.
As punishment for attachment to desirable things,
It is said that Ravana of Lanka was killed.
verses.chinese:
很多大有作为的人们,
既不好胜又会弃邪念;
因为过分的贪得无厌,
据说罗刹因此丢性命。

verses.english:
In both congenial and contentious matters
Deal with great people, never the coarse.
Regarding matters of buying and selling,
Deal with valuables, not deadly concoctions.
verses.chinese:
仁慈和辩论是圣者的所为,
恶劣者绝不会有这种行为;
生意兴隆只能对宝物而言,
却没有人把梅毒当摇钱树。

verses.english:
For adequate revenue, the royal vault is filled
With small taxes, not excessive ones;
Little by little, anthills, beehives,
And the waxing moon become full.
verses.chinese:
国王是通过广泛征税,
少量征收来积满仓库;
如蚁垤蜂蜜和上弦月,
都是积少却成多一样。

verses.english:
A ruler should collect taxes from the populace
In a fair manner that does not oppress them.
If too much of its fragrant resin drips away,
Then the sal tree itself will dry up.
verses.chinese:
国王在不危害百姓之下,
通过运作智慧来征税收;
如娑罗树里蕴藏的香脂,
流得太多也会枯死一样。

verses.english:
Rulers especially must be even-tempered;
It is petty to be angered by trifles.
Even if a snake had a gem on its head,
What sensible person would stand before it?
verses.chinese:
国王特需品性高尚,
不因小事而动大怒;
虽然毒蛇有其宝珠,
哪有明人还敢接近。

verses.english:
Anyone who desires prosperity
Should first and foremost safeguard the Dharma.
How can mere wealth that debases the Dharma
Ever endure, even in this life?
verses.chinese:
尽管是个非常贪财的人,
也应该以人伦道德为上,
败坏道德所得到的钱财,
不可能在世上长久享用。

verses.english:
Do not be overly affectionate, even to friends,
Nor excessively harmful, even to enemies.
Expectations of friends are the basis of disputes;
Retaliation is easy for anyone.
verses.chinese:
即使亲友也不该过分亲近,
就是敌人也不该过分仇恨;
过分要求亲友会结成怨恨,
行凶报复是轻而易举的事。

verses.english:
Gentleness will pacify the temperate
And even quell the uncouth.
Because gentleness can accomplish anything,
The wise say, "Gentleness itself is sharp!"
verses.chinese:
用柔和之法可以攻克柔和,
同样用柔和也能攻克粗鲁;
因为柔和之法能成就一切,
智者都说柔和是至高法宝。

verses.english:
Even if you are disliked by others,
Do not announce, "He is my enemy!"
Or "So and so is unkind to me!"
Mentioning such things exposes oneself.
verses.chinese:
不要声张谁是自己的仇人,
不要埋怨谁对自己不慈悲;
如果把怨声恶气传了出去,
就会造成没有必要的裂痕。

verses.english:
Do not reside in those kinds of places
Where people are oblivious to modesty and shame,
Cannot distinguish between reverence and contempt,
And desire only wealth and food.
verses.chinese:
不会顾忌惭愧和羞耻,
不能区分尊敬和蔑视,
只有挥霍钱财的贪欲,
这种地方不应该久留。

verses.english:
One should not vacate one's original residence
Without properly investigating other places first.
If one's leg is not properly positioned,
When the second leg is raised, one falls down!
verses.chinese:
在不了解新环境之前,
不该丢弃以前的住地;
如一只脚还未站稳前,
抬起双脚必定会摔倒。

verses.english:
Strive to keep behavior low-key;
Being demonstrative usually leads to decline.
If a monkey did not dance,
Why else would a rope be tied around its neck?
verses.chinese:
随时需要掩盖自己的行为,
公开表露往往会遭遇灾祸;
如果猴子真的不善于表演,
怎么会在脖子上套住绳索。

verses.english:
Even if someone does witness wrongdoing,
It should not be discussed with the wrong people.
Common people swear misfortune befalls those
Who talk about bad omens they have seen.
verses.chinese:
就是亲眼看到了灾祸,
不要不分场合地乱讲;
看见恶兆就到处乱讲,
就会把灾祸引到自身。

verses.english:
Of what use are food and riches
That everyone else despises?
What wise individual would crave
The filthy fare of dogs and swine?
verses.chinese:
损人利己得来的钱财,
对于明人不会有诱惑;
如猪狗爱吃肮脏粪便,
可智者哪会有此想法。

verses.english:
Words that strike to the heart of someone
Ought not to be spoken, even to foes.
Just like an echo, the censure of others
Will immediately return to oneself.
verses.chinese:
能击中要害的言语,
是敌人也不应说出;
如同山谷间的回声,
时时有反应的潜能。

verses.english:
If one wishes to harm an enemy,
One must possess good personal qualities.
They will exasperate the enemy
And increase one's own stock of merit.
verses.chinese:
如果想要把敌人制服,
自己首先就要有本领,
这样既能让敌人心服,
也能为自己积累福泽。

verses.english:
First generate the enlightened attitude,
Then quell fierce people with harsh measures.
Those who desire to heal their bodies
Cure disease with bloodletting and surgery.
verses.chinese:
想让恶人变成慈悲者,
只能用暴力来牵制住;
如果想对身体有好处,
就该用放血来驱除病。

verses.english:
Even minor wrongs, when committed,
Must be promptly and persuasively rectified.
Once water starts to flow in a ditch,
Are not flooding gullies then seen?
verses.chinese:
尽管害人的事情非常微小,
也应该迅速地将它消除掉;
如水坝上裂出的小小决口,
也会造成惊涛骇浪的灾难。

verses.english:
The wise do not commit wrongful acts
Even though they know how to do so.
Since elephants destroy their enemies,
See how kings always keep them chained.
verses.chinese:
智者不应该办理的事情,
尽管会做也不会去办理;
虽然大象能够冲破敌阵,
却被国王牢牢缚捆一样。

verses.english:
Do not abandon allies even if they are troublesome;
Do not be nice to enemies even if they are kind.
Crows may harass each other,
But if they rely on owls they are ruined.
verses.chinese:
朋友憎恨时也别抛弃,
敌人仁慈时也别贴近;
虽然乌鸦会互相残害,
靠近猫头鹰就要倒霉。

verses.english:
No matter what size tasks the wise undertake,
They always concentrate on what they do.
The lion is unwaveringly attentive
Whether killing rabbits or elephants.
verses.chinese:
不管是大事还是小事,
智者必定会全力去办;
狮子要杀大象和兔子,
同样对待而绝不马虎,

verses.english:
What wise person would reside somewhere
Where the learned are not respected?
Is it possible to sell crystals
In a land where they are used as flints?
verses.chinese:
不尊重有学问者的地方,
不可能有学者长久停留;
把水晶当作火石的地方,
不可能有人来贩卖水晶。

verses.english:
The wise either explain things to others
Or meditate in secluded forests.
Jewels either adorn crown ornaments
Or remain on remote ocean isles.
verses.chinese:
智者要么向人讲解经典,
要么就在静处修炼佛法;
宝石要么成为高档头饰,
要么仍然会留在海岛上。

verses.english:
There are personal advantages to be gained
From depending on those sages superior to oneself.
The birds who dwell on the slopes of Mount Sumeru
Become as radiant as gold.
verses.chinese:
紧随比自己高明的智者,
必定会对自己产生利益;
生活在须弥山上的鸟儿,
一定会变为黄金的颜色。

verses.english:
One does not achieve greatness oneself
By serving those who are great but jealous.
See how the moon wanes
When it draws near the radiant sun.
verses.chinese:
依靠嫉妒心很强的伟人,
自己也不可能功成名就;
正如月亮离太阳太近了,,
就会出现了盈亏的变化。

verses.english:
Who could possible associate
With any friend who was undependable?
Rainbows in the sky have beautiful colors,
But wishing them as adornments is a fool's delusion.
verses.chinese:
如果对亲友也不肯信任,
就没有人愿和他交朋友;
虽然天上的彩虹很美丽,
只有愚者会当作是装饰。

verses.english:
Whatever one personally dislikes
Should never be done to others;
Think instead of how one feels
When slightly harmed by others.
verses.chinese:
自己不喜欢做的事情,
不要随便强加于他人;
试想一下自己受害时,
究竟有什么样的感觉。

verses.english:
Whenever people bestow on others
What they themselves find pleasing,
Others will treat them nicely in return:
This is the way to be respectful.
verses.chinese:
根据自己的兴趣爱好,
要求别人必须随从你;
别人也用同样的方式,
来要求你也随其所好。
